turns.text: Can we buy the city e-bike battery packs from Brightcell Energy? They quote £104.00.
turns.reply:
I cannot see or change Ledgerline ERP, so I cannot check whether Brightcell Energy is an active supplier, whether we already have a rate contract for city e-bike battery packs, or what status and certificates they currently hold.

However, based on Northbridge policy:

1. **Lithium-cell parts qualification:** Battery packs are lithium-cell parts. Under Purchase Policy (POL-PUR-001 §6.2) and Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003 §4.1), lithium-cell parts may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in Ledgerline, which must be uploaded and verified before the first order is placed. Under Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy (AMD-SUP-2026-02 §1.1), the UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months, with a valid-to date at least 60 days after the date the order is placed.
2. **Supplier status & onboarding:** Orders may only be placed with active suppliers (POL-PUR-001 §6.1). A new supplier must be fully onboarded under POL-SUP-003 before any order can be placed (POL-PUR-001 §6.3).
3. **Price and contracts:** A lower price quote alone is not sufficient. Under Purchase Policy (POL-PUR-001 §6.4), you must "prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part."
4. **Approval limits:** As a purchase executive, your gross order limit is £250,000 including VAT (POL-APR-002 §3.1). Any order above this threshold must go to your manager for approval (POL-APR-002 §5.1).

**Next steps:**
- Check Ledgerline to see if Northbridge already has an active supplier with a rate contract for these battery packs.
- If Brightcell Energy is a new supplier, they must first complete onboarding under POL-SUP-003, provide a qualifying UN 38.3 certificate verified by the senior buyer, and be set to active before any order can be placed.
